stem: Draw the perpendicular bisector of the line segment $AB$ with $A(0, 6)$ and $B(4, 4)$. Drag the two points so the line is that bisector.
solution: Gradient of $AB$: $\frac{4-6}{4-0}=-\frac12$, so the perpendicular gradient is $2$.

hints.text: A perpendicular gradient is the negative reciprocal of the gradient of AB.
Take the reciprocal of the gradient of AB and also change its sign.
The bisector passes through the midpoint of AB. Check that your line goes through it.
Find the gradient of AB and the midpoint of AB first.
